answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, and the bond is slashed if peers catch it copying or spamming. Like a comet, a single fake burns bright and fast, but it cannot return at dawn with a fresh face for free — the deposit is gone. An ivory-tower reputation score alone would fail, because it costs nothing to mint new names; only a bond that hurts to lose turns cheap identities into a real expense for the attacker.
